interaction.trigger: Walk or jump across an opening between any two connected screens

source.representation: Native player projected in one active screen

target.representation: Same player projected into an adjoining Mac or phone screen

relationships.label: Root-connected graph of Mac and numbered phone rectangles

workingState.label: Stable phone identities, rectangle positions and sizes

paths.forward: The same native player crosses a shared opening; each renderer clips its own active region.
paths.reverse: Walk or jump across connected phone screens back to the Mac without replacing the character.
paths.interruption: Cancel a drag when its source rotates or disappears. Atomic topology changes deactivate disconnected components and rescue only stranded characters.
paths.fallback: Disconnect closes the seam and rescues the same player to the Mac; labelled Return to Mac provides recovery.
paths.reducedMotion: No decorative transition; both views draw the current authoritative frame.

identity.commitment: One spawn UUID for one native node.

spatial.commitment: One bottom-left world coordinate system and adjoining rectangles.

context.commitment: Cyan openings and placement diagram explain the relationship.

state.commitment: Velocity, jump state and facing stay native-owned.

control.commitment: Phone and Mac inputs feed one controller.

task.commitment: Continue walking or jumping across either screen.

checkpoints.start: One native character inside Mac region.
checkpoints.midpoint: One ID spans the seam between any two connected screens, clipped by each viewport. Drag ghosts do not change live geometry.
checkpoints.settled: Phone draws same frame and pose while Mac simulation remains authoritative.
checkpoints.reverse: Same native node returns to Mac.
checkpoints.interrupted: Stale inputs released, latest region used, offscreen player rescued if disconnected.
checkpoints.reducedMotion: Identical world and input ownership without decorative effects.
